meta.sources: Reddit (Arctic Shift full-history) + College Confidential; official rates from each school's Common Data Set / UC admit data

counsel.typical: Rising sophomore from a solid four-year (state flagship or mid-tier private/LAC) with a 3.9-4.0 college GPA, often an HS Ivy reject, aiming at CS, applied math, pre-med, or poli-sci.
levers: Tie the why-transfer essay to the open curriculum and your major
Build close ties with 2-3 professors for strong recs
Treat 3.9+ as the real GPA expectation, not 3.85
Keep ECs college-based and cohesive; no national award needed
watchouts: Sub-3.85 admits are rare outliers
A generic why-Brown essay sinks otherwise strong files
counsel.feeders: State flagships (SUNY, UCs, Purdue), mid-tier privates/LACs; some peer laterals

counsel.typical: Freshman or sophomore at a strong public flagship with a 3.9-4.0 GPA, most often econ/business aiming at Tepper, carried by a tight fit narrative rather than ECs.
levers: Take on-major coursework before applying, especially quant/econ for Tepper
Write a specific why-CMU case naming what your school lacks
Going test-optional is fine; the transcript carries the file
Light, conventional ECs are enough with a clean transcript
watchouts: Below high-3.8s needs a documented extenuating explanation
Tepper and SCS are the toughest named gates
counsel.feeders: Strong public flagships (Big Ten, SUNY); California CCs a distinct second channel

counsel.typical: Sophomore reapplicant from a T25-T50 private or flagship with a 4.0, overwhelmingly Economics-bound, often admitted through binding Transfer Early Decision.
levers: Apply binding TED; admits repeatedly credit it as decisive
Post a literal 4.0 freshman year; weak HS GPA is forgiven
Take rigorous major-aligned courses, even upper-division ones early
Focus the why-transfer essay on specific UChicago resources gained
watchouts: Below ~3.7 is exceptional territory
Not a community-college pathway; feeders are four-year schools
counsel.feeders: T25-T50 privates (Emory, Brandeis, Northeastern, Amherst); flagships (UVA, UNC)

counsel.typical: Sophomore or junior from a flagship (Michigan most repeated) or mid-tier private with a ~3.98 median GPA, aiming at Econ/Financial Econ, SEAS, or CS; CC minority routes through GS.
levers: Tie the essay to the Core, NYC, and a concrete program gap
Push into real 300-level major coursework with all A's
From CC, finish a high-GPA AA/AS and target GS
Refine a few applications deeply rather than applying wide
watchouts: Sub-3.7 needs an exceptional essay or distinctive supplement
GS carries a perceived recruiting asterisk for finance
counsel.feeders: Michigan, UVA, SUNYs; Fordham/WashU-type privates; CA CCs into GS

counsel.typical: Rising sophomore from a SUNY, UC, or NYU-type school with a 3.85-4.0 GPA, targeting Dyson, CS/Info Science, or Economics with a clean fit-and-resources story.
levers: Name a specific program - Dyson, ILR, CALS - in your why-transfer essay
Aim at contract colleges (CALS, ILR, Human Ecology) for better odds
Take non-intro major coursework at heavy credit loads
Cultivate 2-3 professors for strong recommendations
watchouts: Dyson and Engineering are the toughest gates
Offers are conditional with a ~3.5/B+ completion floor; some colleges still require tests
counsel.feeders: SUNYs, UCs, NYU CAS, T25-T60 privates; steady CC minority

counsel.typical: Sophomore from a flagship or selective private with a 3.8-4.0 GPA (4.0 modal), econ/math/STEM leaning, running a positive redemption arc after an HS Ivy shutout.
levers: Secure two deep professor letters; shallow recs sink files elsewhere
Write a cohesive why-transfer tying college ECs to the major
Expect the waitlist and stay engaged; many admits come off it
watchouts: Waitlist-heavy path in
Nothing below 3.8 appears; CC feeders are rare
counsel.feeders: UCLA/T100 publics, Emory, Boston College, small LACs; CC rare

counsel.typical: Rising sophomore from a T15-T40 private or flagship with a median 4.0 (16 of 25 exactly 4.0), in Econ, CS, pre-med, or finance-bound Arts & Sciences.
levers: Treat 3.95+ as the real expectation; 3.83 is the lone bottom
Write a fit-specific why-Duke essay tied to the major
College research or a club leadership role or two suffices
Build professor relationships deliberately for recommendations
watchouts: Below 3.9 is a long shot regardless of pedigree
Duke accepts far fewer transfer credits than rivals
counsel.feeders: T15-T40 privates/LACs (Emory, Wake, USC), flagships; ~quarter from CC

counsel.typical: Rising sophomore with a 3.9-4.0 rebuilding after a mediocre HS record, aiming at econ/business (Goizueta, finance goals) or pre-med sciences (NBB, biology).
levers: Carry heavy rigorous loads (18-20 credits, non-intro classes)
Write personal essays naming specific professors, classes, and clubs
Lock in at least one strong professor recommendation
Target Goizueta directly for business/finance goals
watchouts: 3.4-3.7 admits only appear with a compensating hook
A vague transfer rationale is disqualifying
counsel.feeders: State flagships (Rutgers, UF, UGA), CC second-chance track, mid-tier privates

counsel.typical: Rising sophomore or junior with a near-4.0 at a flagship or selective private, trading up into McDonough, econ, government/pre-law, or SFS for the DC pipeline.
levers: Frame a DC-aligned major and career-placement rationale
Aim the file at McDonough, SFS, or CAS econ specifically
Cite the CALL/Capitol Hill program as demonstrated interest
From CC, ride an honors track with PTK and internships
watchouts: Roughly 180 of ~2,500 transfer applicants admitted
Aid packages are often mediocre; compare offers carefully
counsel.feeders: Flagships (UVA, UF, UCLA, IU Kelley); selective privates; CCs a steady third

counsel.typical: Tiny sample (~15 admits, ~0.7% transfer rate): every reported GPA is a 4.0, majors scatter (music/pre-med, physics, English), and admits overlap heavily with Yale.
levers: Assume a flawless 4.0 plus a distinctive academic identity
Treat it as a lottery even with perfect stats; apply to peers
Fall-entry only; plan the cycle accordingly
watchouts: Sub-1% transfer admit rate
Data is too thin to define a profile; hedge everything
counsel.feeders: Too few records to call; admits cross-admit with Yale most

counsel.typical: Sophomore or rising junior with a 4.0-modal GPA from a flagship, LAC, or CA/FL community college, in pre-med/bio, engineering, or econ/poli-sci - and real research depth.
levers: Accumulate substantial research: hundreds of hours, posters, a manuscript
Found or lead an organization tied to one clear through-line
Take rigorous major-relevant courses with Dean's List markers
Write a tight why-transfer connecting every activity to a purpose
watchouts: BME is brutally competitive; many get redirected to ChemBE
Nothing below the high-3.8s appears among traditional admits
counsel.feeders: Ohio State/UIUC-type publics, Emory and top LACs, CA and FL CCs

counsel.typical: Tiny sample (~11 admits, ~2.4% rate): reported GPAs 3.98-4.0, math/physics leaning, Stanford the most common cross-admit; MIT says no formula and takes all college types.
levers: Carry a near-perfect GPA in hard math/physics coursework
Any college type works, including community college
Plan around the GIRs; expect limited credit carryover
watchouts: ~2% transfer admit rate
Tiny-n data; profile claims are low-confidence
counsel.feeders: Too few records to call; admits from all college types including CCs

counsel.typical: Sophomore or junior with a median 3.92, entering LSA for CS or Economics, drawn evenly from community colleges, state schools, and mid-tier privates.
levers: Polish essays and recs hard; admits credit them over ECs
Carry a real STEM/upper-level course load; test-optional is fine
Apply CS through LSA and the Advanced Selection route
Want business? Enter LSA Econ, then attempt internal Ross transfer
watchouts: Ross is a separate, much harder admit
Out-of-state and international full-pay cost is the real obstacle
Sub-3.5 needs a documented explanation and upward trend
counsel.feeders: Even split: CCs (CA, Michigan), state schools (MSU, UM-Dearborn), T30-T50 privates

counsel.typical: Rising sophomore with a median 4.0 from an NYU/Northeastern-tier private or strong public, in Economics or CS, transferring for academic fit and recruiting.
levers: Name a concrete NU resource (program, lab, curriculum) in the essay
Take 15-20 credit rigorous loads with prereqs fully completed
Build two or three professor relationships for letters
Skip EC panic; several admits had literally none
watchouts: Sub-3.7 admits carried unusual hooks (1590 SAT, arts supplement)
Many admits arrive via the waitlist
counsel.feeders: NYU (top feeder), Northeastern, Emory, Vanderbilt; strong publics; CA CCs

counsel.typical: Sophomore from a four-year school (IU Kelley the repeat feeder) with a 3.88-4.0, business/econ/finance-bound toward Mendoza with open IB/consulting goals.
levers: Post 3.9+ over 30+ graded credits at dean's-list level
Secure deep professor recommendations; shallow ones cost admits elsewhere
Give a clear fit reason: size, class sizes, business support
Average essays are survivable; the transcript and recs carry
watchouts: No community-college feeders appear; a CC file is a long shot
Mendoza admission is not guaranteed; some land in Arts & Letters
counsel.feeders: IU Kelley (repeat), UCLA-type flagships, Wake Forest/Santa Clara privates; no CCs

schools.name: Princeton
majors: math/physics (with interest in political science/public policy)(1)

counsel.typical: First- or second-year with a high-3.8s GPA from an honors community college or strong four-year, in quant/STEM (math, ORFE, EE) or policy/pre-law tracks.
levers: Write a course-specific why-Princeton essay naming actual classes
From CC, use the honors program as the rigor signal
Show quantitative coursework fit for ORFE/EE tracks
Land strong letters of recommendation
watchouts: Tiny transfer intake; the realistic pool is near-Ivy caliber cross-admits
counsel.feeders: Honors community colleges; four-years whose students cross-admit at Ivies

counsel.typical: Sophomore with a 3.9-4.0 from a state flagship or California CC, in CS, engineering, or business/finance, drawn by aid and the residential-college fit.
levers: Complete every major prerequisite; missing ones trigger auto-rejects elsewhere
Show research or solid campus involvement in the major
Write a specific why-transfer tied to concrete academic goals
Lean on the aid/cost and close-knit-culture angle
watchouts: Below ~3.7 requires standout essays or an unusual story
CS/engineering have hard prerequisite and credit-transfer gates
counsel.feeders: State flagships (UNC, UT Austin, UIUC, UVA, Alabama); CA and other CCs

counsel.typical: California community-college junior with a 3.9-4.0, honors standing, and a deliberate HS-underperformance-to-CC-redemption arc, often first-gen, in CS or poli-sci.
levers: Run the full CC honors track: AA-T, Dean's List every semester
Frame the essays around the HS-to-CC turnaround story
Reachable on-campus ECs (tutoring, student government) are enough
For CS, add some research or technical-project exposure
watchouts: Below ~3.9 is under the visible bar
Stingy credit and major access; pre-med/impacted majors often mean four full years
counsel.feeders: California CCs (Pasadena City, Palomar) dominate; some UCLA/UC laterals

counsel.typical: In-state California CC junior with a ~3.88 GPA, IGETC and major prereqs done, entering Letters & Science for Economics, Political Science, or Business.
levers: Complete IGETC and all lower-division prereqs with A's
Revise PIQs relentlessly with multiple reviewers
Target ~3.94+ for Haas and ~3.97+ for CS/EECS
Protect the transcript: a late D, NP, or W risks rescind
watchouts: Haas and EECS/CS are effectively near-4.0 tracks
No admission guarantee exists (unlike UCLA TAP)
Competitive median is 3.85-3.90 despite the lower floor
counsel.feeders: CA CCs (~86%: Santa Monica, De Anza); UC Riverside-led UC laterals

counsel.typical: In-state California CC junior with a ~3.90 GPA on a planned TAP/IGETC pipeline, in poli-sci, econ/business econ, or psychology; ~87% of admits come from CCs.
levers: Finish IGETC and every major-prep course with no gaps
Get TAP-certified through your CC honors program
Rewrite PIQs for months; admits credit them over everything else
For impacted STEM/econ majors, sit at 3.9-4.0
watchouts: Impacted majors (CS, data, econ, engineering) demand 3.9+ and zero prep gaps
Non-California or four-year origin lacks transfer priority - steep climb
counsel.feeders: CA CCs (Santa Monica by far, PCC, DVC); some UC-to-UC laterals

counsel.typical: Sophomore or junior with a 3.9-4.0 from a community college (PTK common) or public flagship, overwhelmingly aiming at Economics, with business a distant harder gate.
levers: Apply to Econ/Arts & Sciences, not Kenan-Flagler, as the realistic path
Bring full transferable loads (60+ credits, honors enrollment)
Hold A-level grades through matriculation; rescission worry is real
Show college-based leadership: PTK office, club president, research
watchouts: Kenan-Flagler admits only ~30 transfers a cycle - a reach for nearly everyone
Sub-3.7 admits are exceptions leaning on holistic factors
counsel.feeders: CCs (California, Miami Dade Honors) and publics (UC Irvine, NC State, UMD)

counsel.typical: Rising sophomore or junior with a 4.0 from a mid-tier private (Emory, Tufts, NYU) or flagship, in CAS Economics, pre-med/public health, CS, or Wharton-finance hopes.
levers: Treat a 4.0 as the modal expectation
Deliberately build 2-3 professor relationships; recs are decisive
Write the earned-my-way-up why-Penn narrative tightly
Engineering-minded? Enter through CAS - SEAS takes no external transfers
watchouts: No external transfers into SEAS
Community college is a clear minority path (LPS aside)
counsel.feeders: Emory (repeat), Tufts, NYU, elite LACs; UVA/Michigan flagships; CC rare

counsel.typical: Rising sophomore with a 4.0 (52 of 86 reported GPAs) from NYU, a UC, a flagship, or Kelley, in econ/business/finance, transferring for a smaller close-knit campus.
levers: Complete the first-year track prereqs for your lane
Name courses, professors, and clubs in the why-transfer essay
Get 1-2 strong professor letters
Stay ready for late-spring waitlist waves
watchouts: Heavily waitlist-driven; many admits come in late waves
Below ~3.7 is rare and needs an exceptional fit story
counsel.feeders: NYU CAS, UCs (UCLA most), flagships, IU Kelley, peer privates; ~20% CCs

counsel.typical: Near-4.0 student after 1-2 years, most often from a community college honors track or big public, in Political Science/pre-law, often first-gen with a turnaround arc.
levers: Max available rigor: CC honors, dean's list, completed prereqs
Build focused campus-leader ECs: student government, a founded club, editing
Name specific Yale resources and explain the academic turnaround
Frame two or three linked academic interests, not one
watchouts: Sub-3.85 essentially never appears
Eli Whitney (EWSP) is a separate nontraditional-age track
counsel.feeders: Community colleges dominant (honors programs); state flagships and Big 10 second
